atomicity.reason: One obligation - the state of a single warning output as a function of the spread - with set and clear as the two halves of the same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: 'the computed temperature spread' is a reference to a quantity computed in another requirement; the reader cannot tell from this requirement what the spread is a spread of.
comprehensibility.suggestion: Restate the input inline, e.g. 'the difference between the highest and lowest valid cell temperature', or reference SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA explicitly.

feasibility.reason: A single threshold comparison on an already-computed figure is trivial and contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR owns the imbalance verdict raised on a spread above 8 K; this requirement pins that threshold and both output transitions.

unambiguity.reason: Behaviour is undefined for a cycle in which no spread exists - SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA publishes no figures when no valid temperature sample is present - so the output in that cycle reads either as held or as cleared.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define the warning's value when the spread is unavailable, e.g. 'when no spread is available the warning shall be reported as unavailable' rather than cleared.

verifiability.reason: The 8 K threshold and its boundary are exact, but 'in every cycle' names no period, so the required response time of the warning cannot be tested.
verifiability.suggestion: State the cycle explicitly, e.g. 'once per 100 ms cycle', matching SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA.

summary: The 8 K threshold matches the parent, but the requirement leans on a spread it does not define, never names its cycle, and says nothing about the cycle in which SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA publishes no spread at all.
